issues.description: ALTER TABLE DROP contract loses the structural distinction between DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT branches.
issues.detail: The two new DROP forms are folded under a single outer 'DROP' keyword with inner Delimited(Sequence(...)). A caller (rule, formatter, fixer) walking the parse tree must now disambiguate by peeking at the next keyword rather than dispatching on a named subtype. The supertype contract 'an ALTER TABLE action is identifiable by its head' is weakened. Consider distinct alter_table_action subtypes for column vs constraint drops.

issues.description: Removing the outer Delimited around ALTER TABLE actions silently narrows the supported grammar.
issues.detail: Previously ALTER TABLE accepted a comma-delimited list of actions (the very example removed from the fixtures used this). The new OneOf accepts exactly one action. This is a postcondition weakening relative to T-SQL's ADD column_b ..., DROP COLUMN ... form. If that form is genuinely invalid in T-SQL, document it in a code comment; if not, the contract has been narrowed without a written justification.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar accepts a SignedSegment on the increment, leaking a parser convenience into the type's value space.
issues.detail: IDENTITY(seed, increment) in T-SQL requires both to be integers, but the increment cannot be the same negative-zero-vs-min-int special case the seed needs. Allowing SignedSegmentGrammar on both positions is fine for parsing but the ADT now admits values the underlying engine rejects. A short comment stating 'parser is permissive; semantic validation deferred' would make the contract explicit.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment without a stated rationale in the grammar.
issues.detail: Adding numeric language IDs (lcid) to DEFAULT_LANGUAGE is correct per T-SQL, but the option list grammar now silently encodes 'language is identifier-or-string-or-number'. A one-line comment near _default_language documenting that the numeric form is the LCID would keep the contract legible for future maintainers.

issues.description: TableIndexSegment added to DECLARE @t TABLE body without a fixture exercising it alongside a column-level index.
issues.detail: The new fixture covers the standalone-index case but the existing fixture already has 'name varchar(128) NULL index _name (name)' (column-level index). The two index forms now coexist in the grammar; an explicit combined fixture would lock in that both substitute correctly inside the same DECLARE body. Cheap insurance against future regressions.

review.summary: The PR is a careful parser extension and the new fixtures demonstrate the intended forms. From an abstract-data-type lens, two concerns are worth addressing. First, the ALTER TABLE rewrite collapses the old outer Delimited and re-folds DROP COLUMN/DROP CONSTRAINT under a shared DROP head, which both narrows the accepted surface and erodes the structural distinction between action subtypes — downstream rules now disambiguate by lookahead rather than by named node. Second, the IDENTITY and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE grammars admit a slightly larger value space than the engine accepts; a short comment stating the parser-is-permissive contract would keep the spec honest. The new test coverage is good but a combined column-index plus standalone-index DECLARE fixture would pin down substitutability of the two index forms.
